description.en: 86 familiar breeding birds of Sweden and the Nordic countries. Front: the English name and the official Swedish name; back: the scientific name. Scientific and English names follow the global checklist AviList (v2025b; BirdLife Sverige's lists follow AviList v2025, whose names v2025b leaves unchanged). Names from Wikidata and Dyntaxa, checked against AviList and BirdLife Sverige's official Swedish list.
description.sv: 86 välkända häckfåglar i Sverige och Norden. Framsida: det engelska namnet och det officiella svenska namnet; baksida: det vetenskapliga namnet. Namnen kommer från Wikidata och Dyntaxa och är kontrollerade mot AviList och BirdLife Sveriges officiella Sverigelista.

method: Scope and authority. The library editor asked for about 80 common Nordic birds, English and Swedish name on the front and the scientific name on the back, verified against the IOC World Bird List and BirdLife Sverige. Research showed that the IOC list made its last update with version 15.2 (13 April 2026) and its editors now work on AviList, the unified global checklist first released on 11 June 2025 (current version v2025b, 11 June 2026), and that BirdLife Sverige's Taxonomic Committee decided to 'fully adopt and endorse' AviList for its Swedish lists. AviList v2025b was therefore chosen as the single taxonomic authority for scientific and English names, and BirdLife Sverige's lists (which follow AviList) for the Swedish names.

Candidate list. The authoring agent wrote down 123 candidate scientific names of familiar Nordic birds from general knowledge, including the newer combinations it expected (for example Cyanistes caeruleus, Poecile montanus, Linaria cannabina, Astur gentilis) and the older Accipiter gentilis to see how the sources treat it.

Wikidata (content source). One SPARQL query (the first query below) fetched, for every candidate name, the items with that taxon name (P225), their taxon rank (P105), English and Swedish labels and aliases, and Dyntaxa id (P1939). All 123 names matched an item of rank species (Q7432). The raw response was saved.

AviList (authority, verification). The AviList v2025b short and extended spreadsheets were downloaded and each candidate's species row was looked up by exact scientific name, recording Sequence, Authority, English_name_AviList and the decision summary, and from the extended file the protonym. Corvus cornix and Accipiter gentilis have no species row: AviList treats the Hooded Crow as part of Corvus corone and the goshawk as Astur gentilis.

BirdLife Sverige (verification). The official Swedish list 2025 (Förteckning över Sveriges fågeltaxa, version 2025, which states that it follows AviList) was downloaded; for each candidate its species row gave the Swedish and English names, and the category (A–E) and status (H = breeding) were read from the species row when it has them (monotypic species) or else from the subspecies rows that follow it (the species row of a polytypic species has no category or status); the evidence quotes the rows separately. As a second check the official Swedish names of all the world's birds (version 2025, file NL2025b.xlsx, following AviList v2025) was downloaded: for all 86 species in the deck its Swedish and English names equal the Swedish list's. BirdLife's lists follow AviList v2025; AviList states that v2025b changed no English or scientific names.

Dyntaxa (content source). Each of the 86 selected species was looked up in Dyntaxa, the Swedish taxonomic database of SLU Artdatabanken, through its CC0 dataset on GBIF (species search restricted to the dataset, exact canonical name, then the record's vernacular names, which come in Swedish (swe) and English (eng)). All 86 are ACCEPTED under exactly the deck's scientific name and each has the deck's Swedish name among its Swedish vernacular names; 83 have the deck's English name, in the same letter case, among their English vernacular names (the other three: 'European Crested Tit', 'Long-tailed Bushtit', 'Chaffinch'). For the 13 species whose genus changed, the record's synonyms were fetched as well.
Selection. The candidates were filtered by the criteria in the selection section and cut to 86 by editorial judgement; the exclusions and their reasons are listed there.

Card text. Front, English: taken from the content sources, choosing among the English names they carry the one that is AviList v2025b's English name: Dyntaxa's English vernacular name (CC0) for 83 species, and for crested tit, long-tailed tit and chaffinch, whose Dyntaxa English names differ, the Wikidata label or alias ('Crested Tit', alias of Q207831; 'Long-tailed Tit', label of Q170831; 'Eurasian Chaffinch', label of Q25383). Every English front is therefore exactly AviList's name, in AviList's capitalisation, and also present verbatim in a CC0 source. Front, Swedish: Dyntaxa's Swedish vernacular name that is the official BirdLife Sverige name, in lower case (it is also the item's Swedish Wikidata label, letter case aside in three cases). Back: the scientific name, tagged as Latin: the AviList name, which is also the Wikidata taxon name (P225) and the accepted Dyntaxa name. No Swedish text was translated by the agent: every Swedish name is the official BirdLife Sverige name.

Former names. For the 13 species whose genus changed (tits formerly in Parus, finches formerly in Carduelis, and Coloeus, Curruca, Astur, Lyrurus and Chroicocephalus), a back note gives the former combination. Each note is backed by the Dyntaxa synonym list and by a Wikidata taxon synonym or alias or the AviList protonym; the Wikidata queries are below (two first attempts timed out and were simplified).

Cross-checks. During authoring, scripts compared every card's Wikidata taxon name and labels with the AviList species row, the Swedish list row, the NL2025b row and the Dyntaxa record, and the names with the final IOC World Bird List, v15.2 (https://www.worldbirdnames.org/IOC_Names_File_Plus-15.2.xlsx, downloaded 2026-10-04, licensed CC BY 3.0 Unported): every card's scientific, English and Swedish names agree across AviList, the Swedish list, NL2025b and Dyntaxa, and with Wikidata except for the letter-case differences recorded under quality control; all 86 scientific and English names are identical to IOC 15.2's. Those authoring scripts were not recorded verbatim, so in quality-control round 3 one cross-check script (crosscheck.py, run with the last command in the queries) was written and run over the final dossier. For every card it compares, as exact case-sensitive strings: the English front with AviList's English_name_AviList (short xlsx, sheet 'AviList v2025b short', rows with Taxon_rank 'species', keyed by Scientific_name), with IOC 15.2's English name (first sheet, rows whose rank column is 'Species', keyed by the scientific-name column), with the English column of the Swedish list's species row and of NL2025b's row of rank 'art', and with the record's Dyntaxa English vernacular names (live GBIF, language 'eng'); the Swedish front with the Swedish list, NL2025b and Dyntaxa's Swedish vernacular names (language 'swe'); and that the species row or one of its subspecies rows (an unindented binomial followed by indented trinomials of the same binomial) has category A or C with status H. All comparisons pass for all 86 cards except that Dyntaxa lacks the English front of the three cards named in step 8, which Wikidata supplies (and the builder checks). The IOC list is used only for this comparison; nothing in the deck comes from it, and as the builder has no CC BY 3.0 Unported licence entry, its download is recorded under the AviList source, whose editors succeeded it.

Machine checks. Each card carries a Wikidata check of its taxon name (P225), and checks of its English and Swedish names as a label or alias wherever Wikidata has the text in exactly the card's letter case. The builder runs them against live Wikidata on every build.

Process. Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
selection: The deck has 86 bird species that are widespread, familiar breeding birds of Sweden, most of them also common in Norway, Finland and Denmark: garden and woodland songbirds, crows, woodpeckers, owls, raptors, waterfowl, waders, gulls and terns, and grouse. Inclusion criteria: (1) a species in AviList v2025b, the global checklist the Swedish lists follow since June 2025; (2) in BirdLife Sverige's official Swedish list 2025 in category A or C with breeding status H (two species, Canada Goose and Common Pheasant, are category C, introduced and established); (3) an accepted species in Dyntaxa with the same Swedish name; (4) a Wikidata item whose taxon name (P225) is the AviList name, whose Swedish label is the official Swedish name and whose English label or an alias is the AviList English name (in both cases letter case aside); together with Dyntaxa's English and Swedish vernacular names, every name on the cards is then present in a CC0 source in exactly the card's spelling and letter case (English: Dyntaxa for 83 species, a Wikidata label or alias for the other three; Swedish: Dyntaxa for all 86). The 123 candidates were drafted by the authoring agent from general knowledge of the Nordic avifauna (no published list of common birds was copied), and the list was then cut to 86 by the agent's editorial judgement of how familiar a species is to a Nordic beginner. Left out because of taxonomy or naming: Corvus cornix (Hooded Crow; in the Swedish list the subspecies Corvus corone cornix, gråkråka, of the species Corvus corone, kråka): AviList treats it as part of Corvus corone (Carrion Crow), so neither the name Corvus cornix nor the English name Hooded Crow is a species name under the deck's authority, and the Swedish list no longer has it as a species; Acanthis flammea (Redpoll, gråsiska): AviList treats Common, Lesser and Arctic Redpoll as one species named 'Redpoll'; a recent and contested lump; Anas crecca (kricka): AviList includes the American Green-winged Teal and names the species 'Green-winged Teal', while Wikidata calls it Eurasian Teal: the English side would be ambiguous; Delichon urbicum (hussvala): AviList's English name 'Western House Martin' is neither a label nor an alias on Wikidata (which has 'Common House Martin'); Emberiza schoeniclus (sävsparv): AviList's 'Common Reed Bunting' is not on Wikidata, which has 'Reed Bunting'; Glaucidium passerinum (sparvuggla): AviList's 'Eurasian Pygmy Owl' is not on Wikidata, which has 'Eurasian Pygmy Owlet'; Fratercula arctica (lunnefågel): a regular visitor but not a breeding bird in Sweden (status T in the Swedish list); Accipiter gentilis: not a separate card: AviList, the Swedish list and Dyntaxa place the goshawk in Astur, and the deck has it as Astur gentilis. Left out only to keep the deck near the requested size of about 80 (they met criteria 1, 2 and 4; Dyntaxa was only consulted for the species kept): Turdus viscivorus, Loxia curvirostra, Coccothraustes coccothraustes, Corvus frugilegus, Nucifraga caryocatactes, Anthus pratensis, Anthus trivialis, Riparia riparia, Phylloscopus sibilatrix, Sylvia borin, Curruca curruca, Muscicapa striata, Saxicola rubetra, Streptopelia decaocto, Strix uralensis, Milvus milvus, Branta leucopsis, Gallinula chloropus, Actitis hypoleucos, Gallinago gallinago, Larus marinus, Tetrastes bonasia, Alca torda, Oriolus oriolus, Alcedo atthis, Lagopus lagopus, Lagopus muta, Cinclus cinclus, Motacilla flava. Subspecies are not included. Former scientific names are given as a back note (not as an answer) on the 13 cards whose genus changed.

licensing: The deck is released under CC0 1.0. Its content comes from two CC0 sources: Wikidata (structured data released under CC0) for the item behind every card, its taxon name and its English and Swedish labels, and Dyntaxa (published by SLU Artdatabanken on GBIF under CC0 1.0) for the accepted scientific names, the Swedish and English vernacular names and the former names. Every string on the cards is present verbatim, in the same letter case, in Dyntaxa or Wikidata (English names: Dyntaxa for 83 cards, Wikidata for 3). AviList (CC BY 4.0) and BirdLife Sverige's lists (no licence stated, so treated as all rights reserved) were used for verification only: they confirmed which of the names carried by the content sources is current and official, and no text, list or selection was copied from them. Species names are facts, and the deck's selection of species is the authoring agent's own. AviList is still credited in the deck's provenance and in this report; the IOC World Bird List (CC BY 3.0 Unported), consulted as an extra check, contributed nothing.
